A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPE model-selection work. Their main text, figures, table, equations, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original Hopper experiments comparing selectors, including gap, misspecification, coverage, feature-variant, and rollout-count studies in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original Hopper experiments and their outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: LSTD-Tournament, its feature variants, and the regression-based and sign-flip selectors retain their procedures and objectives. The new discussion of alternative instrumental variables concerns future work, not an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Hopper-v4 with the same gravity/noise grids, misspecified candidate sets, and good, poor, and mixed data-coverage conditions. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The model-free comparisons retain random selection, TD-square, average Bellman error, BVFT, and mb_naive. The model-based comparisons retain random selection, mb_naive, and the Zitovsky, Antos, and sign-flip selectors alongside LSTD-Tournament.

E3.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix D retain the absolute OPE-error metric, data collection, policy settings, and candidate configurations. The experiments still use up to 3200 transitions, ordinarily 128 Monte-Carlo rollouts, horizon 1024, and 15 or 5 candidate models.

E4.justification: Sections 6.2–6.3 and Appendix E retain the same gap and misspecification sweeps, coverage tests, LSTD feature-variant comparisons, and small-rollout studies. The added mathematical counterexample in Appendix B is theoretical evidence rather than a new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions describe bootstrap resampling with replacement and report mean performance with 95% confidence intervals in Section 5.2. No additional run counts, seeds, statistical tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: The matched experimental plots retain their curves, confidence bands, rankings, and reported findings. v2 Figures 1–4 correspond to v3 Figures 2–5, and Appendix Figures 6–11 retain their results; no experimental result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a four-point stochastic-transition counterexample to the naive prediction loss: the true model has expected Euclidean loss 1 + sqrt(2)/2, exceeding sqrt(2) for an incorrect deterministic-zero model. The existing propositions, theorems, and proofs otherwise retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about guaranteed selectors, the controllable simulation-based experimental protocol, and promising Hopper performance. The claimed statistical-rate advantage over BVFT and the scope of the preliminary empirical conclusions are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly interprets LSTDQ as instrumental-variable regression, identifies the left feature vector in Equation (3) as the instrument, and proposes exploring alternatives. Existing result interpretations and limitations concerning candidate realism and coverage are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-repository URL at the start of Section 6, whereas v2 provides no equivalent access information. Appendix D retains the existing implementation, environment, policy, hardware, and runtime details.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Bradtke and Barto, Chen et al., and Sajed et al. Appendix A newly distinguishes Sajed et al.'s groundtruth-simulator value estimation from this paper's selection across candidate simulators, while Section 7 connects LSTDQ to instrumental-variable research.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations and the publication footer, clarifies 'dynamics models' in the abstract, adds acknowledgements, and inserts several short explanatory paragraphs. The main section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The pipeline diagram moves from v2 Figure 5 at the appendix opening to v3 Figure 1 in the main text, with slight resizing and corresponding page-flow changes. Most intermediate equation numbers in the appendix derivations are removed; existing plots and Table 1 retain their content and basic structure.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses limited explanation, attribution, and access gaps through the explicit bias counterexample, clearer discussion of related Monte-Carlo work, and a code-repository link. Moving the pipeline diagram near the problem setup also improves accessibility. These are useful refinements, while the methods, main guarantees, experimental evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
